title: Specimen Collection, Handling, Transport & Storage

references.label: CLSI Standards for Clinical Laboratory Practice
WHO Laboratory Quality Management System Handbook

purpose: To collect, label, transport, and store clinical specimens in a way that preserves analyte integrity from the point of collection to the point of testing.
principle: Analytes and cells begin changing the moment a specimen leaves the patient — metabolism continues in whole blood, cells lyse, pH and gas tensions shift, and organisms may proliferate or die off. Correct collection order, container/anticoagulant choice, gentle mixing, temperature control, and prompt transport are all aimed at freezing the specimen's condition as close as possible to its in-vivo state until it can be processed.
requiredMaterials: Correct collection container/tube for the ordered test
Labels printed or written per local policy
Insulated transport container with temperature control as required
requiredReagents: Skin antiseptic appropriate to the specimen type (e.g. for blood cultures, per that protocol)

procedure.instruction: Positively identify the patient using at least two identifiers before collection, and confirm the request matches the specimen to be collected.

procedure.note: The order of draw itself is method/standard-dependent — follow your laboratory's current CLSI-based order rather than a memorized universal sequence.
procedure.instruction: Select the correct container/tube and anticoagulant for each ordered test; when multiple tubes are drawn, follow the laboratory's specified order of draw to avoid cross-contamination between additives.
Label every specimen at the bedside/point of collection, before leaving the patient, with the identifiers the laboratory requires.
Mix anticoagulated tubes by gentle inversion the specified number of times — never shake, which can hemolyze cells or foam/denature protein.

procedure.note: Consult the laboratory's specimen requirements/handling manual per analyte — no single time/temperature rule applies to every test.
procedure.instruction: Transport specimens to the laboratory within the time and temperature window specified for each test (e.g. some analytes require immediate chilling, others must not be refrigerated).
Process (e.g. centrifuge, separate serum/plasma) within the specified time window; store appropriately if testing is delayed.

observations: A properly handled specimen arrives correctly labeled, within its stability window, without visible hemolysis/clotting (unless clotting is expected, e.g. serum tubes), and at the required temperature.
interpretation: Any deviation from required identification, container, timing, or temperature is a pre-analytical variable that can invalidate downstream results even if the analytical run itself is performed correctly.
precautions: Treat every specimen as potentially infectious.
Never relabel a specimen away from the patient based on memory — mislabeling at collection is not correctable afterward.
limitations: This entry describes general handling principles; exact tube types, order of draw, and stability windows are method/analyte-specific and defined by the testing laboratory's procedure manual, not universally fixed values.
biosafetyNotes: Standard/universal precautions apply to all specimen handling; use appropriate PPE and follow the facility's exposure-control plan.
